```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(mgcv)
```


# Problem 1 

## Importing and tidying the data 

```{r}
homicide_df = 
  read_csv("data/homicide-data.csv") |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
   mutate(
    city_state = paste(city, state, sep = ", "), 
    solved = as.numeric(disposition == "Closed by arrest"), 
    victim_age = as.numeric(victim_age)
  ) |> 
  filter(city_state != "Dallas, TX", 
         city_state != "Phoenix, AZ",
         city_state != "Kansas City, MO", 
         city_state != "Tulsa, AL", 
         victim_race == "White" | victim_race == "Black"
         )  
```

## Writing a glm function 

```{r}
city_glm = function(obs_city) {
  
  homicide_df |> 
    filter(city_state == obs_city) |> 
    glm(solved ~ victim_age + victim_sex + victim_race, data = _, family = binomial()) |> 
    broom::tidy(conf.int = TRUE) |> 
    filter(term == "victim_sexMale") |> 
    mutate(
      OR = exp(estimate), 
      ci_l = exp(conf.low), 
      ci_h = exp(conf.high)
      ) |> 
    select(term, OR, ci_l, ci_h)

}
```

```{r}
city_glm("Baltimore, MD") |> 
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Mapping across every city in the dataset 

```{r}
results_df = 
  homicide_df |> 
  distinct(city_state) |> 
  mutate(results = map(city_state, city_glm)) |> 
  unnest(results)
```

## Making a plot 

```{r}
results_df |> 
  mutate(fct_reorder(city_state, OR)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = city_state, y = OR)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_l, ymax = ci_h)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    x = "City",
    y = "Adjusted OR (male vs. female victims)",
    title = "Odds of solving homicides with male vs. female victims"
  ) 
```

Cities with odds ratios of more than 1 mean that homicides with male victims are more likely to be solved. Cities with odds ratios of less than 1 mean that homicides with female victims are more likely to be solved. In most cities, homicides with female victims are more likely to be solved because the odds ratio is less than 1. Interestingly, cities with odds ratios higher than 1 often have larger confidence intervals.

# Problem 3 

## Importing data 

```{r}
birthweight_df = 
  read_csv("data/birthweight.csv") |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  mutate( 
    babysex = case_match(
      babysex, 
      1 ~ "male", 
      2 ~ "female"
      ), 
    frace = case_match(
      frace, 
      1 ~ "White", 
      2 ~ "Black", 
      3 ~ "Asian", 
      4 ~ "Puerto Rican", 
      8 ~ "Other", 
      9 ~ "Unknown"
    ), 
    malform = case_match(
      malform, 
      0 ~ "absent",
      1 ~ "present"
    ), 
    mrace = case_match(
      mrace, 
      1 ~ "White",
      2 ~ "Black", 
      3 ~ "Asian", 
      4 ~ "Puerto Rican", 
      8 ~ "Other"
    )
    )
```

## Making a model for birthweight 

```{r}
smooth_mod = gam(bwt ~ s(fincome) + s(gaweeks), data = birthweight_df)
```

I was interested in using family monthly income and gestational age as predictors of birthweight. I used a smooth fit to model this relationship. 

```{r}
birthweight_df |> 
  add_predictions(smooth_mod) |> 
  add_residuals(smooth_mod) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = pred, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "Fitted birthweight (g)", y = "Residual (g)")
```

## Other models 

```{r}
main_effect_mod = lm(bwt ~ blength + gaweeks, data = birthweight_df)
interaction_mod = lm(bwt ~ bhead * blength * babysex, data = birthweight_df)
```

## Comparing with cross validation 

```{r}
cv_df = 
  crossv_mc(birthweight_df, 100) |> 
  mutate(
    train = map(train, as_tibble),
    test  = map(test, as_tibble)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    smooth_fit = map(train, \(df) gam(bwt ~ babysex + s(fincome) + s(gaweeks), data = df)),
    main_effect_fit = map(train, \(df) lm(bwt ~ blength + gaweeks, data = df)),
    interaction_fit = map(train, \(df) lm(bwt ~ bhead * blength * babysex, data = df))
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    rmse_smooth = map2_dbl(smooth_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_main = map2_dbl(main_effect_fit, test, rmse),
    rmse_interaction = map2_dbl(interaction_fit, test, rmse)
  )
```

```{r}
cv_df |> 
  select(starts_with("rmse")) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "model", 
    values_to = "rmse",
    names_prefix = "rmse_") |> 
  mutate(model = fct_inorder(model)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = model, y = rmse)) + geom_violin()
```

My hypothetical model is terrible. It does not compare with the other two models. The interaction model is by far the best of the three.
